title: Documented filters, one sort convention, and strict rejection of unknown parameters
iWant: declared filter names, a single sort syntax, and hard errors on anything the endpoint does not understand
soThat: my queries do exactly what they say or fail loudly, never silently returning the wrong result set

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every collection endpoint's filter parameters are declared in the generated spec with their types and accepted values; no undocumented filter is honoured.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the generated spec entry for a collection endpoint
acceptanceCriteria.when: its declared filters are compared with the parameters the implementation honours

acceptanceCriteria.description: Sorting uses ?sort=field,-field2: comma-separated keys, leading minus for descending, applied in declared key order.
acceptanceCriteria.then: results order by fieldA ascending then fieldB descending

acceptanceCriteria.description: A request carrying an unknown query parameter is rejected with 400 and a problem-details body naming the unknown parameter, on every endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request carries an undeclared query parameter
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 400 with the declared error envelope naming the parameter, and no handler logic runs

acceptanceCriteria.description: A sort key that is not declared sortable for the resource is rejected with 400 and a problem-details body naming the key and the declared sortable set.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 400 with the error envelope naming the key and the sortable fields

acceptanceCriteria.description: A filter value violating the parameter's declared type or format is rejected with 400 and a problem-details body naming the parameter and expected type, never coerced silently.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a declared filter of a specific type
acceptanceCriteria.when: a value of the wrong type is submitted
acceptanceCriteria.then: the service responds 400 with the error envelope naming parameter and expected type

acceptanceCriteria.description: Filters, sorting, and pagination compose: a filtered, sorted collection paginates correctly with the filter and sort preserved across cursor navigation.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a filtered and sorted multi-page query
acceptanceCriteria.then: subsequent pages honour the same filter and sort without restating them incorrectly or losing them
